**Resolved / Related Issues**
Items resolved / related issues by this PR.
- Closes #6737

**Details of Changes**
Add details of changes here.
- Disables the button with a short delay before re-enabling.

**Validation**
How did you test these changes?

**Screenshots (optional)**

**Comment**
I was thinking maybe we could use events (as opposed to the delay) to restore the button once the RefreshItems() method had completed. But as it is running on a different thread I don't believe that is possible?
pr_comments:
> > I was thinking maybe we could use events (as opposed to the delay)
> 
> There are a couple of options:
> 
> 1. Use the second parameter of RefreshItems, it's a callback that is executed after folder has finished reloading. Use Dispatcher.RunAsync to change IsEnabled property on the correct thread.
> 
> ```cs
> appInstance?.FilesystemViewModel?.RefreshItems(null, async () =>
> {
>     await Dispatcher.RunAsync(Windows.UI.Core.CoreDispatcherPriority.Normal, () => RestoreDefaultButton.IsEnabled = true);
> });
> ```
> 
>  2. Add an overload of the RefreshItems that returns a Task that you can `await`
> 
> ```cs
> public async Task RefreshItems(string previousDir)
> {
>     await RapidAddItemsToCollectionAsync(WorkingDirectory, previousDir, null);
> }
> ```
> 
> So the RestoreDefaultIcon method becomes (no need for delay):
> 
> ```cs
> await CoreApplication.MainView.DispatcherQueue.EnqueueAsync(async () =>
> {
>     await appInstance?.FilesystemViewModel?.RefreshItems(null);
> });
> ```
> 
> With option 2 there's also the possibility to set enabling of the button directly from XAML by doing domething like: `IsEnabled="{x:Bind RestoreDefaultIconCommand.IsRunning, Converter={StaticResource BoolNegationConverter}, Mode=OneWay}"`

I think I like option 2 best. I’ll work on implementing that. Thanks for your advice and help on these PRs.
@puppetsw I see you went with option 1 at the end? Curious: were there issues with option 2?

> @puppetsw I see you went with option 1 at the end? Curious: where there issues with option 2?

Ahh if I remember correctly it was something with the overloaded method and being async. Just ended up being easier to use the callback method. 

Edit: I could go back and implement option 2 if you like. I have time to do it tonight.

https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/17484252/140539999-90ab8bfc-ccae-4cd3-b517-5194eb19c149.mp4
